## **Since Everyone Has Access To Increasingly Capable AI, Where Is Your Differentiation?**


When it comes to AI, B2B marketing leaders often focus on chatbots, prompts, content creation and agentic use cases, and model selection. Those topics are understandably relevant and where most of my AI client conversations begin. But in my experience, they aren’t usually where lasting impact comes from.


## **What Does AI Know About Your Organization’s Go-To-Market Strategy?**


In a world where AI trust, hallucinations, and difficult-to-quantify results continue to persist, more mature organizations are raising a critical question (or at least I’m guiding them there): *How do we improve what AI knows?*


I’m seeing an increasing strategic mindset gap: on the one hand, leaders who focus on ensuring access to AI tools and pushing for more use cases to test while, on the other, leaders who are taking a more strategic approach by ensuring that AI knows about their business, customers, and markets before they push for broad use.


## **Two Proprietary Knowledge Examples Illuminate The Future**


Consider what[Thomson Reuters](https://www.thomsonreuters.com/en/press-releases/2026/august/thomson-reuters-leverages-its-world-class-data-assets-to-launch-its-own-frontier-model) and[Wolters Kluwer](https://www.wolterskluwer.com/en/news/wolters-kluwer-transforms-trusted-legal-content-into-structured-v2) are doing for their customers. Their AI vision started with this: Trusted knowledge became the central point of their AI efforts, delivering incredible value to their clients — knowledge that a public LLM would not have access to.


AI did not create those assets. It compounded their value. Their knowledge was always important. AI made it possible to operationalize that knowledge at a scale, speed, and level of accessibility that was not previously practical. But the lesson is bigger than Thomson Reuters and Wolters Kluwer. As AI becomes commonplace, the organizations that stand out will not necessarily be those with access to better AI models. Instead, the real leaders will bring more of their own[proprietary or “private” knowledge](https://www.forrester.com/blogs/the-private-ai-model-explosion/) into their AI, enabling far more effective AI-led and AI-augmented work.


## Proprietary Knowledge Becomes The AI Advantage For B2B Marketing


The lesson for B2B marketing leaders is to seize a similar opportunity. Every marketing organization has proprietary knowledge that public AI models do not: accumulated buyer understanding, commercial intelligence, strategic assumptions, competitive insights, and years of institutional learning. These knowledge assets shape the decisions that matter most, from identifying high-value customers and recognizing buying signals to prioritizing markets, allocating investment, and competing effectively. Public AI models do not know those things. Your organization does.


Competitors can purchase similar tools, access similar models, and use similar prompts. They cannot replicate decades of accumulated customer understanding, market insight, decision-making experience, and institutional learning.


## **Make AI Smarter About Your Business**


The marketing organizations that will gain the most from AI may not be those with the best underlying model usage. They are likely to be those that are best at transforming proprietary knowledge into repeatable and scalable organizational capabilities with private AI. In that future, AI’s ability to leverage your proprietary knowledge becomes a critical differentiator and efficiency lever.


Leaders should ask not “Which AI should we use?” but “What unique knowledge can we make available to it?” Forrester clients, please reach out to[schedule an inquiry](https://www.forrester.com/inquiry) with me to discuss how to enable AI with your proprietary knowledge.
